A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, research questions and principal experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reward-model bias experiments, calibration and instruction-following evaluations, and appendix ablations for PPO-M, PPO-C and CDPO.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional confidence/logit analyses, loss comparisons and reward-averaging ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 changes a central component of PPO-C: the threshold-selected adjustment proportional to absolute reward becomes an adjustment proportional to reward minus its exponential average. Default w changes from 0.5 to 2.0. The original rule survives as the threshold variant in Appendix E.9; PPO-M and CDPO objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training-data collections, RewardBench, six calibration evaluation datasets, MT-Bench and Arena-Hard. The added diagnostics and ablations use retained coverage, including TruthfulQA; Arena-Hard was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated Eq. 1+2 reward-model-loss comparator against Eq. 2 alone in Table 14 and explicitly compares threshold-based and difference-based PPO-C in Table 15. The principal SFT, PPO, PPO†, DPO and DPO† comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Under the revised PPO-C rule, default w becomes 2.0 instead of 0.5. V2 adds controlled alpha sweeps over 0, 0.1 and 1.0 and confidence-position log-probability inspection. Existing dataset splits, model checkpoints, training budgets, DA/CoT evaluation procedures and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds confidence-distribution and confidence-token-logit analyses, averaging-factor ablations for both PPO-C variants, and a combined-loss study with training curves. It also expands reward-rule comparisons and revises the sensitivity and combined-method analyses, substantially increasing scrutiny of the method's design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The added confidence-score and logit distributions describe model outputs rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: All PPO-C metric entries in Table 1 change, alongside its Table 2 scores and the combined-method results. For example, Llama3 GSM8K CoT ECE changes from 0.2252 to 0.1546, while MT-Bench changes from 8.05 to 7.87, under the revised method and coefficient. V2 also adds diagnostic and ablation results; main PPO-M and DPO results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the calibrated reward in Eq. 3 changes from a piecewise threshold rule to a reward-minus-average product; the previous definition is retained as Eq. 5. The other principal losses remain equivalent, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of reward-model bias toward high confidence, calibration through PPO-M/PPO-C without additional golden labels, preservation of task and conversational capabilities, and extension to CDPO. Added evidence and the revised PPO-C implementation do not materially change these broad claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets confidence-token logits as evidence against random confidence-number generation and explains alpha's stability–adaptation tradeoff. Its coefficient-selection rationale prioritizes calibration at w=2.0 despite conversational-score reductions, whereas v1 favors w=0.5 to preserve capabilities. The stated DPO limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies reward extraction at the EOS token, identifies the exponential-average input as a batch mean, and documents initialization in the alpha ablation. Hardware, most training hyperparameters and the code-release information were already provided in v1.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and the positioning relative to supervised calibration, prompting, RLHF and DPO remains substantively unchanged. Related-work revisions primarily rephrase existing discussion.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites paragraphs throughout the introduction, methods, experiments, related work and appendices. It also adds acknowledgment and reproducibility sections and reorganizes the expanded Appendix E, going beyond isolated copyediting.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn for the revised reward rule, and Figure 6 replaces a small rejected-response comparison with two four-mode panels. V2 adds Figures 22–24 and several ablation tables, reformats prompt examples, and revises captions and layout. Existing Figures 20–21 retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: V2's additional diagnostics, reward-rule comparisons and averaging-factor ablations make important design choices easier to assess. The gain is limited by calibration–capability tradeoffs and an inconsistency in the new loss ablation: Table 14's Eq. 2 baseline reproduces threshold-PPO-C values rather than the PPO-M values in Table 1, weakening that comparison.
